newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firmer and at recent highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firmer and at recent highs.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled at their highest level in five-weeks amid fresh fund buying, floor sources said.
The buying, noted most heavily in the October contract, continued to erode steady selling by producers and fueled October to a life-of-contract high of 11.20 cents.
July climbed to a five-week high of 11.35 cents.
Light producer and trade selling is expected to provide resistance at each tick higher, market sources said.
"There is some steadiness in Thai premiums but a lot of selling around from Brazil," a broker said.

The July contract closed 0.17 cent firmer at 11.34 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.13 to 11.35 cents. October settled 0.19 firmer at 11.19 cents, while the deferred contracts ended 0.14 to 0.08 cent higher.
Firm resistance was pegged at 11.50 cents in July, but producer-linked selling should limit gains before that level, dealers said.
They added that today's gains were technically-driven while noting the lack of reinforcement from the fundamental side.
In addition to a dearth of substantial physical offtake, Mexico said it could produce a record crop in 1996/96, depending on rain-induced milling delays.
As of May 24, Mexico had produced 4.289 million tonnes of refined, raws and browns, from 39.697 million tonnes of cane, the Agriculture Ministry's Agroindustry Sugar Committee, said.
Output reached a record 4.377 million tonnes last season.
Open interest in most-active July fell by 1,229 lots to 73,042 lots as of early Friday, CSCE said.
An estimated 25,649 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 22,977 lots.
